description: Prefixes, suffixes, case vowels and particles for Linear A morphological analysis. ventris_propagate.py tries each prefix and suffix by its `form` when it strips a word.

evidence: JA-KI-SI-KI-NU = yaksīkin (3ms G imperfect)
JA-RA = yara (impf. 3ms of √y-r-h)
JA-PA-RA = yapʾara (3ms volitive)
JA-TA-I-*301-U-JA (AP Za 1), the 3ms of the A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA paradigm
A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA = ʾatainawaya (1cs tG of √n-w-y)
A-SA-SA-RA-ME = ʾaššaram, with ʾa- for the ya- of yaššaram
A-DU = Addu (but this may be a complete word)

prefixes.function: conjunction u- 'and' + h-n presentative 'behold'; /h/ elided as in Ugaritic w hn > wn (Watson 1996, 285–87; Lipiński 1997, §27.25). Arabic hunna is the 3fp pronoun 'they' (Fischer 2002, §264), not a presentative.
evidence: U-NA-KA-NA-SI = wannā kanāsī 'so, behold my gathering!'
U-NA-RU-KA-NA-SI = wannā lū kanāsī 'and behold, may my gathering [take place]' (with precative RU/lū)
Cognates: Ugaritic w hn / wn 'and behold'; Hebrew wəhinnē; Amarna u annû (EA 253:18–20)
prefixes.note: Hebrew hinnēnī 'here I am' (Gen 22:1, 22:11) is the speech-act parallel: announcing presence before the divine.

prefixes.function: precative/optative particle ('may, let there be'). R/L neutralized in Linear A. Appears between presentative U-NA- and verb stem. Converts declarative to petition.
evidence: U-NA-RU-KA-NA-SI vs U-NA-KA-NA-SI — same root √k-n-s, different speech act (optative vs declarative)
Ugaritic l- (precative before verbs), Akkadian lū, Hebrew lū (conditional/optative)
prefixes.note: Only attested after U-NA- prefix (3 occurrences: IOZa16, PKZa11, PKZa12). Never appears without preceding presentative. The distribution confirms it modifies the modal force of the following verb rather than functioning as an independent morpheme.

evidence: possible prosthetic vowel before consonant clusters

prefixes.function: 2nd-person or 3fs prefix; person/gender requires an ending or context
evidence: Semitic t-prefix; conditionally TA-NU-MU-TI = /ta-nʿum-u-tī/ if TA begins the damaged word
TA-NA-RA-TE-U-TI-NU = tan-raṣē-u-tī-n(u) and TA-NA-I-*301-U-TI-NU = tan-ʿinā-u-tī-n(u), where TI marks the 2fs
MI-NU-TE = minūt (fem.)
SI-RU-TE

suffixes.function: HT104-final element: possible suffix or repeated classifier; exact function unresolved
evidence: DA-KU-SE-NE on HT103 beside DA-KU-SE-NE-TI on HT104 favors suffixation
DA-KU-SE-NE-TI, I-DU-TI, and PA-DA-SU-TI share the same pre-quantity position on HT104
GORILA I 171 allows final TI to be an ideogram or classifier
suffixes.note: The base/extended DA-KU-SE-NE pair supports added morphology, but HT104 alone does not determine gender or case. Finkelberg 2002/03, 96–97 proposes dative/recipient ‘for/to’; an ablative ‘from’ is not established. It is not stripped: HT104 does not yet separate a suffix from a classifier.

evidence: KU-PA₃-NA-TU = Kubānatu (fem. of Kubānu)

suffixes.function: possible emphatic/topical clitic; other functions remain context-dependent
evidence: JA-SA-SA-RA-MA-NA: provisional /yašaram=na/, compared with Ugaritic -n or -(Vn)na
KU-PA₃-NU = Kubānu (-ānu)
QE-DE-MI-NU = Qadmīnu (-īnu gentilic)
DA-KU-SE-NE = Takušenni
KA-DU-MA-NE = Qadmān

suffixes.function: mimation, with E as a support vowel
evidence: JA-SA-SA-RA-ME = /yaššaram/
U-NA-KA-NA-SI = wannā kanāsī

case_vowels.description: Semitic tripartite case system — final vowel encodes grammatical case. Speculative for Linear A but consistent with NWS grammar.

evidence: KU-PA₃-NU, Kubānu, ends in -NU
final -U common in Linear A words
final -A common
rare word-final vowel in corpus, consistent with marked genitive
